findingClass: the pull walk re-asks fields and REWRITES them with identical values, which is indistinguishable in every downstream reading from the walk confirming them -- a healthy-looking write rate that is entirely no-op churn, and the field_sources provenance trail it produces is noise that hides the one real change in it
failThreshold: RECOMMENDED, NOT MEASURED: on a data-job cycle with no newly-filed documents and no genuine source disagreement, (field_sources rows written this cycle) / (ipo_field_plan rows re-asked this cycle) stays under 5%.
unverifiableWhen: no data-job cycle ran since the previous audit, OR ENABLE_FIELD_PLAN_WALK is off in the slot being audited, OR ipo_field_plan holds no rows for the window
retiredReason: same ratio as pull_noop (design §4 PULL-NOOP row: writes per cycle over fields re-asked per cycle) -- the only difference was an ENABLE_FIELD_PLAN_WALK gate, and that gate made the check WEAKER, not stronger: the nightly audit process (scripts/vps-data-audit-cron.sh) is not shown to carry the scraper's runtime flags, so this check would read UNVERIFIABLE every night regardless of whether the walk actually ran. pull_noop already treats a 0-reask denominator as UNVERIFIABLE ('a walk that did not run is not a quiet walk'), which covers the exact case this check's env gate was meant to catch, with no dependency on the audit process seeing the scraper's environment.
note: Retired 2026-09-24 (item 10 review round): the design's own §4 table lists one check for this ratio, PULL-NOOP. This entry duplicated it under a second id with a weaker gate; removed rather than kept alongside pull_noop.
